It did so regardless of the inner URL's scheme, `blob` included. Each `blob:` prefix cost one stack frame, with no limit on nesting depth. `Url::parse()` accepts a URL with 10,000 `blob:` prefixes followed by `https://example.com/` (50,020 bytes in total); calling `Url::origin()` on it overflowed the default 2 MiB stack of a spawned thread.\n\nA stack overflow aborts the whole process, and `catch_unwind()` does not catch it. One such URL crashes any program that calls `Url::origin()` on untrusted input. `url::quirks::origin()` also calls `Url::origin()`. For example, Servo's `URL.origin` DOM getter calls `url::quirks::origin()`, so a script on a page can trigger the overflow.\n\n`url` 2.5.9 follows the URL Standard: `Url::origin()` takes the origin of the inner URL only when its scheme is `http`, `https`, or `file`, returns an opaque origin otherwise, and never calls itself. functions mark unwritten bytes as initialized when given a zero-length buffer","description":"The extended-attribute functions in `rustix::fs` (`getxattr`, `lgetxattr`, `fgetxattr`, `listxattr`, `llistxattr` and `flistxattr`) write into a `Buffer` and then mark as many bytes initialized as the system call reported. When the buffer has zero length, the operating system treats the call as a size query: it writes nothing and returns the size of the attribute value or of the name list. rustix still marked that many bytes as initialized.\n\nPassing a `Vec` whose length equals its capacity through `spare_capacity` gives such a zero-length buffer, and rustix then set the vector's length past its capacity over memory that was never written. and related constructors violate I/O safety","description":"`tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd` provides safe constructors (`new`, `with_interest`, `try_new`, and `try_with_interest`) that accept any `T: AsRawFd` rather than requiring proof of ownership or validity of the file descriptor. Because `RawFd` implements `AsRawFd`, safe code can construct an `AsyncFd` from an arbitrary or closed file descriptor, or close/replace the underlying file descriptor while the `AsyncFd` is still alive.\n\nThis violates I/O safety in two ways:\n\n1. `AsyncFd<T>` implements `AsFd` for all `T: AsRawFd` by calling `BorrowedFd::borrow_raw(self.as_raw_fd())`, allowing safe code to obtain an arbitrary `BorrowedFd<'_>` without owning the file descriptor.\n2. Tokio's I/O driver stores a pointer to an internal allocation in the `epoll`/`kqueue` user data for registered file descriptors. If the underlying file descriptor is duplicated and then closed while an `AsyncFd` is alive, and the OS reuses that file descriptor number for a another IO resource on the same runtime, dropping the first `AsyncFd` deregisters the reused file descriptor number and frees the first while the original file description remains registered in `epoll`, leading to a use-after-free when a readiness event fires.\n\nStarting in Tokio 1.51.6, 1.53.3, and 1.54.0, `AsyncFd::new`, `AsyncFd::with_interest`, `AsyncFd::try_new`, and `AsyncFd::try_with_interest` are deprecated in favor of the `unsafe` constructors `AsyncFd::register` and `AsyncFd::register_with_interest`. Callers must ensure that the file descriptor remains valid, open, and unchanged for the lifetime of the `AsyncFd`.","date":"2026-10-13","aliases":[],"related":[],"collection":"crates","categories":["memory-corruption"],"keywords":["io-safety","use-after-free"],"cvss":null,"informational":"unsound","references":["https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/issues/8538","https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/issues/8539"],"source":null,"url":"https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8587","withdrawn":null,"license":"CC0-1.0","expect-deleted":false},"affected":{"arch":[],"os":[],"functions":{"tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd::new":[">=0.3.2"],"tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd::try_new":[">=1.37.0"],"tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd::try_with_interest":[">=1.37.0"],"tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd::with_interest":[">=0.3.2"]}},"versions":{"patched":[">=1.51.6, <1.52.0",">=1.53.3"],"unaffected":["<0.3.2"]}}],"yanked":[{"kind":"yanked","package":{"name":"async-executor","version":"1.14.0","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index","checksum":"c96bf972d85afc50bf5ab8fe2d54d1586b4e0b46c97c50a0c9e71e2f7bcd812a","dependencies":[{"name":"async-task","version":"4.7.1","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"concurrent-queue","version":"2.5.0","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"fastrand","version":"2.5.0","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"futures-lite","version":"2.6.1","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"pin-project-lite","version":"0.2.17","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"slab","version":"0.4.12","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"}],"replace":null},"advisory":null,"affected":null,"versions":null}]}}
